final_answer: Depth-first search (DFS) explores a graph by going as deep as possible along each branch before backtracking, while breadth-first search (BFS) explores all immediate neighbors level by level. DFS uses a stack (or recursion), and BFS uses a queue. DFS can find a path quickly in deep graphs but may miss shorter paths, whereas BFS guarantees the shortest path in unweighted graphs. Choose DFS for puzzles/mazes, topological sorting, or memory-sensitive scenarios; choose BFS for shortest-path problems, peer networks, or when the solution is near the root.
